text.en: A 5 m ladder leans on a wall with its foot 3 m from the wall. How high does it reach? A right-angled triangle hides inside this picture.

In a right-angled triangle the side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, the longest side.
Pythagoras theorem: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides, c squared = a squared + b squared.
For the ladder, height squared = 5 squared - 3 squared = 25 - 9 = 16, so the height is 4 m.
The converse: if c squared = a squared + b squared in a triangle, then the angle opposite c is a right angle.
Common Pythagorean triples are 3, 4, 5; 5, 12, 13; 8, 15, 17 and 7, 24, 25.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse makes two triangles similar to the whole, which gives another proof.

problem.en: Is a triangle with sides 7, 24 and 25 right-angled?

text.en: The longest side is 25, so test 25 squared against 7 squared + 24 squared.

why.en: The hypotenuse must be the longest side.

text.en: They are equal, so by the converse the triangle is right-angled.

why.en: The right angle is opposite the side of length 25.
